metadata.scope: Public rustia project readiness, based on the current workspace and canonical design docs.
notes: Percentages are rough engineering estimates, not automated metrics.
The scope tracks public rustia crates, conformance, benchmarks, docs, tooling, and release readiness.
Project pillars and non-goals are canonical in design/02-pillars.md.
The public host-bridge remains generic; grabby-specific types and effect catalogs stay outside public rustia.

benchmark_adapters.note: mlua-lua54 runs separately from mlua-luau because both mlua-sys builds use links = "lua"; mlua-luau-jit is an explicit execution mode in the mlua-luau adapter family.

memory_safety.failure: catchable atomic OutOfMemory after one forced collection
memory_safety.telemetry: live, reserved, and optional instruction-boundary peak bytes

mixed_heap_pressure.wasm_linear_memory: constant throughout the warmed second half

decision_reset.preserves: VM configuration, host services, extensions, installed host functions/modules, lifetime memory peaks, and host-owned immutable compiled modules
decision_reset.discards: guest globals, heap objects, coroutines, loaded programs, caches, coverage, tracebacks, and retained roots
decision_reset.restarts: RNG, logical time, instruction counters, compatibility GC state, and deterministic collection scheduling
decision_reset.retained_handle_rule: all Function, Exports, and RetainedValue leases are epoch-checked and stale after reset

typed_invocation.schema: lifetime-independent HostSchema plus a freshly borrowed HostContext per invocation
typed_invocation.authority: sealed Input, Slots, Effects, and SlotWrites views; profile-gated HostMut access
typed_invocation.budgets: one shared fuel budget plus bounded record count and logical record bytes
typed_invocation.commit: per-host-call savepoints and outer publication after guest execution, snapshotting, and typed conversion
typed_invocation.hard_abort: fuel, OOM, record overflow, yield-boundary violations, missing dispatch, and host panic
typed_invocation.panic_recovery: contain host functions, typed dispatch, extension ops, stdout/clocks, and loadstring compiler; discard records and poison the VM until decision reset
typed_invocation.rollback_scope: staged records only, not guest heap/global state, HostMut mutation, or host interior mutability

live_values.handles: rooted Value, Table, and Function handles with VM identity and decision-epoch checks
live_values.payloads: binary strings, buffers, vectors, rich table keys, and functions
live_values.graphs: shared/cyclic table identity, mutation, iteration, and raw equality
live_values.invocation: live arguments and results across ordinary and typed invocations
live_values.snapshot_rule: OwnedValue stays acyclic and reports cycles explicitly
live_values.quota_rule: root-registry admission is logical-live quota checked and atomic

wasm_target_bench.note: The recurring wasm target runner executes rustia, koto, and rhai on Node/V8; the earlier four-runtime matrix is retained as historical portability evidence.

wasm_dispatch_bench.note: The recurring dispatch check runs on Node/V8; historical cross-engine evidence also found call_ref slower than br_table.

bounded_fuzz.vm_limits: 2 KiB input, 4,096 fuel, recursion depth 32, and 512 KiB logical-live memory
bounded_fuzz.toolchain: stable 1.95.0 smoke; nightly-2026-04-06 and cargo-fuzz 0.13.2 remote campaigns
bounded_fuzz.differential_oracle: Luau 0.709 in an isolated bounded worker
bounded_fuzz.remote_campaign: All six targets, including expanded stateful coverage, passed at 347b0af7557535227d7b901713f0e3559c621b02: 30 minutes each plus two-hour stateful/differential extensions; no reported crashes, timeouts or mismatches
bounded_fuzz.rollout: Complete: Rustia #34, WOTS #6, civfun #44 and Grabby #1027 merged after final acceptance gates; all consumers verified against aee98e7815460c2df014c9b20f92de8de5382814

wasm_runtime_ci.tests: bare no-default-feature host adapters, the shared mixed-heap pressure lifecycle, and default web-live adapters

overall_goals.name: Whole public rustia project
overall_goals.state: The architecture is locked and production crates are substantial: the safe-Rust VM/compiler, pending-free pinned conformance corpus, host-pluggable output/time services, host-owned canonical-identity require resolution/cache, lifetime-safe per-invocation host contexts, bounded transactional effect journals, graph-preserving rooted live Value/Table/Function handles with live globals, quota-aware table construction, snapshot-free live serde, a coherent chunk execution API, atomic extension/module installation with fresh lazy dependency cohorts, CLI, benchmark matrix, private HotIR, closure-call PIC, generation-safe object/program reclamation, VM-owned memory telemetry, maintained logical-live quota accounting and script counters, atomic catchable OOM, epoch-safe decision reset, exact dedicated-Linux native plus wasm quota evidence, and a shared native/Node-V8 mixed-heap pressure gate are in-tree. The remaining release gates are safe function construction, semantic-tail hardening, and packaging.
overall_goals.future_plan: Complete safe function construction; then continue semantic-tail hardening, measured optimization, and public release work.

overall_goals.name: Usable embedded scripting crate
overall_goals.state: The facade now includes typed eval/exec, a composable load/source_name/environment builder with owned/live/serde/install terminals, owned scalar/table conversions, host-owned canonical-identity require resolution with per-install cohorts, a lifetime-independent HostSchema with fresh borrowed HostContext values per invocation, capability-specific host views, shared fuel, bounded transactional record publication, usage receipts, rooted live Value/Table/Function handles that preserve rich payloads and graph identity, live globals, quota-aware table construction, owned-key/live-value insertion, VM/decision-epoch-safe exports, owned-value serde plus snapshot-free live deserialization, atomic extensions and installation, host-owned replacement, epoch-safe decision reset, examples, diagnostics, migration guidance, host-pluggable stdout/clock services, VM-owned memory telemetry, maintained logical-live accounting, and configurable quotas. Safe function construction remains before this is a complete rich embedding boundary.
overall_goals.future_plan: Complete safe function construction, diagnostics, and API stabilization.

overall_goals.name: Full public standalone Luau engine release
overall_goals.state: The Luau 0.709 standalone target and pending-free 511-ref conformance denominator (493 Luau 0.709 plus 18 offline PUC 5.1.5 compatibility refs) are strong. Bounded generation-safe object/program lifetimes, VM-owned live/reserved/peak telemetry, maintained logical-live memory limits and script counters, atomic catchable OOM, host-owned require resolution with fresh installation cohorts, transactional module installation, lifetime-safe typed invocations with transactional records, graph-preserving rooted live values with snapshot-free serde, versioned deterministic reset/module lifecycles, and the shared native/Node-V8 mixed-heap pressure gate are implemented; native Linode plus wasm quota evidence is exact. Release still requires remaining live-object ergonomics, semantic-tail/diagnostic hardening, the full correctness/golden target matrix, and packaging. Analyzer/typechecker, raw C API, Roblox, Lua 5.4, and bytecode compatibility are not runtime-release requirements.
overall_goals.future_plan: Close the remaining host-boundary gates, harden the semantic tail and cross-target goldens, then package and publish against the pinned target.

overall_goals.name: Standalone benchmark OSS project
overall_goals.state: Harness, package metadata, split notes, machine-readable inventory, current-results JSON, generated claim gate, history, a standalone target-first current-results HTML report with interpreter-only and best-mode rankings plus cold-start costs, five default workload families, 19 workload entries with cross-adapter #15 string-building source coverage, an in-place #12 array-mutation probe, and six synthetic/realistic memory probes, all 12 requested adapters plus a verified mlua/Luau JIT mode, exact ephemeral-Linux fixed-throughput and evidence-only memory protocols, a recurring wasm target runner for rustia+koto+rhai on Node/V8, retained cross-engine wasm evidence, a call_ref versus br_table dispatch microbench, and an explicit dedicated-Linode native-plus-wasm matrix lifecycle are present.
overall_goals.future_plan: Split from the workspace, add the interop/serde/fuel-limit tranche and regression alerts, and accumulate longer-run public history.

overall_goals.name: Public release readiness
overall_goals.state: License, generated crate metadata audit, explicit internal dependency versions, release-preflight-enforced examples, migration guidance, CLI/diagnostics, typed owned values and callbacks, graph-preserving rooted live values, true-root epoch-safe retained handles, host signature/fuel metadata, output/time services, VM memory telemetry, maintained logical-live limits and script counters with atomic OOM, versioned decision reset, a shared native/Node-V8 mixed-heap pressure gate, release-readiness and semver policy, hosted CI, benchmark claim gating, package dry-runs, and publishability auditing are present; crates are still workspace-private and release polish is incomplete.
overall_goals.future_plan: Close remaining live-object ergonomics and semantic-tail gates before removing publish blockers in topological order.

entries.name: Compiler
entries.state: The production compiler emits bytecode for the pinned corpus and discovers captured bindings before final lowering, enabling direct immutable captures while preserving mutable loop/backedge semantics. Stable preflight now runs a deterministic 2,048-case mutated frontend sweep in addition to the seed corpus and dedicated coverage-guided targets.
entries.future_plan: Add Luau-oracle differential cases and longer coverage-guided campaigns for runtime-error-phase parity, then harden diagnostics, O2 passes, superinstructions, and optimization boundaries.

entries.name: Bytecode dispatch core
entries.state: The portable big-match/br-table interpreter is authoritative. Bounded private HotIR numeric tracelets preserve logical fuel, deterministic-GC policy, and atomic fallback; a four-lane prototype-polymorphic call-site PIC plus direct immutable captures now accelerates the tracked closure workload.
entries.future_plan: Extend verified HotIR effect/control-flow coverage, add profile-led superinstructions/O2 and hot/cold split, and keep fuel, GC, coverage, and fallback semantics invariant.

entries.name: Value representation
entries.state: The sealed 16-byte tagged value, 13-byte inline binary strings, and shared compiled-string references are implemented, documented, and validated by an exact 512-VM Linux sampler.
entries.future_plan: Keep the representation sealed while extending external allocator/RSS measurement history and continuing GC work.

entries.name: Heap and GC
entries.state: Standard uses paced gc-arena debt collection, DeterministicSim uses instruction-count full cycles, weak tables are swept, and tables/functions/upvalues/runtime strings/userdata/buffers/vectors plus loaded programs use generation-safe reusable slots. Retained host values are true roots, while suspended coroutine frames follow the reachability of their public handle through a fixed-point mark; explicit quiescence reclaims obsolete programs/coroutines and releases spare backing capacity. Reset ABI v1 reuses allocation containers while discarding the complete guest heap and loaded-program state at an idle decision boundary. Maintained heap/program/control live accounting backs logical-live quotas and script counters without a whole-VM census at ordinary instruction boundaries; exact live/reserved telemetry and optional peaks remain available. Forced-collection retry and atomic catchable OOM are implemented. Cohort safe-memory-588b541 supplies 99 native Linode samples and a wasm32 512 KiB quota/recovery pass. A shared native/Node-V8 test covers 96 decision epochs and 3,072 rich mixed-heap waves with bounded roots, weak/cyclic reclamation, module replacement, stale handles, exact reset plateaus, OOM recovery, and stable warmed wasm linear-memory pages.
entries.future_plan: Tune collection intervals against the maintained pressure gate and extend external allocator/RSS history.

entries.name: Tables/metatables
entries.state: Broad table, metatable, iteration, and stdlib behavior is conformance-covered. Logical deletion preserves tombstone insertion semantics, larger hash parts use a deterministic side index, and shape-revalidated positive string-slot caches cover global/index reads and writes plus dedicated GETTABLEKS, SETTABLEKS, and NAMECALL field/method paths. Exact OOP candidate ns/unit is 65.959% lower under its accepted Linux protocol; that comparison also includes the weak-table GC-scan correction. A mutation-version-keyed length-border cache was exactly gated on dedicated Linux and reverted after measuring no win on the dense or sparse workloads; quiescent trailing-nil release now bumps the table mutation version for sort-guard coherence.
entries.future_plan: Keep the full suite and exact protocol green, then broaden adaptive specialization.

entries.name: Functions/coroutines/pcall
entries.state: Functions, closures, varargs, coroutines, and protected calls have broad coverage.
entries.future_plan: Keep stackless recursion and yield paths covered as runtime changes.

entries.name: Base/math/string/bit32/vector/utf8 stdlib
entries.state: Major pinned Luau stdlib surfaces, including buffer, vector, utf8, and string pack/unpack behavior, are fixture-covered. Exact buffer.readf32/writef32 and readf64/writef64 round trips preserve NaN sign/payload bits through raw deterministic ingress; f32 uses an explicit cross-target payload mapping while arithmetic results remain canonicalized. Host-environment output/time services are provider-backed: print composes tostring/__tostring into a host stdout sink (no-op without one), no-arg os.time/os.date read a wall-clock provider with a pinned-epoch fallback, and os.clock reads a monotonic provider with a deterministic logical-clock fallback. collectgarbage('count') and gcinfo now report the maintained VM-owned logical-live KiB estimate.
entries.future_plan: Keep the language-library corpus and mixed-heap pressure gate green without treating logical-live or wasm-page evidence as process RSS or allocator parity.

entries.name: Error/debug behavior
entries.state: Host-facing typed errors provide bounded immutable executed-source reports, expression spans, logical callers, factual operation explanations, parser-proven missing block endings, typed host causes, one-based serde paths, module loading context, and console source mapping. Guest error strings and protected-call behavior remain unchanged. Rustia PR32 passed full correctness/conformance, canonical release preflight, platform/Node-V8 CI and remote screening. Client adoption is recorded in WOTS PR5, civfun PR43/CIV-75 and Grabby PR1025; their PR records retain validation and delivery evidence.
entries.future_plan: Continue oracle runtime-error-phase parity coverage and real-host/browser goldens without changing guest errors for presentation; source reconstruction after guest string rethrows and general transpiler mapping are not promised.

entries.name: f64/libm/canonicalization discipline
entries.state: Deterministic number policy is documented and partly enforced by tests.
entries.future_plan: Keep compiler and VM on the same libm/canonicalization rules.

entries.name: Runtime profiles
entries.state: LuauCompat, ReproducibleStandard, and DeterministicSim are concrete runtime profiles. LuauCompat selects Luau-style hash iteration; DeterministicSim omits collectgarbage/gcinfo and optional loadstring, registers the os table iff a deterministic clock provider is plugged, admits a stdout sink on any profile, rejects nondeterministic clock providers, deterministically sweeps weak tables, and rejects external-state/nondeterministic host registrations. Typed invocations make fuel, OOM, record overflow, yield-boundary violations, missing dispatch, and host callback panic hard aborts without changing legacy catchable-OOM behavior. Reset ABI v1 defines a replay-stable idle boundary: host configuration survives, guest state is discarded, deterministic counters restart, and retained handles are epoch-invalidated.
entries.future_plan: Keep the replay, memory, and host-fuel ABIs versioned and cross-target tested.

entries.name: Fuel and limits
entries.state: Instruction fuel exists; legacy roots receive their configured per-execution budget, while a typed invocation shares the lower of its explicit InvocationLimits fuel and the builder/settings ceiling across every guest call. Public host-function fuel metadata carries an ABI version. Reset ABI v1 restarts logical execution and deterministic GC counters. VmSettings::memory_limit_bytes and RustiaBuilder::memory_limit_bytes cap maintained VM-owned logical live bytes with identical native/wasm semantics; quota admission avoids a whole-VM census, pressure forces one collection before a catchable OutOfMemory, and large table/string/buffer requests plus growing table writes are rejected atomically. The shared 96-epoch native/Node-V8 pressure test maintains a 2 MiB quota, proves catchable atomic recovery from an 8 MiB request, and verifies continued allocation afterward.
entries.future_plan: Keep optimized instruction costs replay-stable and maintain the shared native/wasm pressure gate.

entries.name: Cross-engine wasm proof
entries.state: Production rustia wasm and call_ref vs br_table dispatch are measured across V8, JavaScriptCore-family, and SpiderMonkey; the pre-lock wasm gate is closed.
entries.future_plan: Keep the measurements fresh as the wasm artifact and runtimes evolve.

entries.name: Full target correctness and golden matrix
entries.state: Linux x86_64, macOS arm64, and wasm/V8 golden evidence exists, with retained JavaScriptCore-family and SpiderMonkey shell portability measurements. Hosted CI cross-compiles the portable engine library for the full declared native triple set plus wasm32 and executes bare plus default web-live wasm adapter tests on Node 22/V8. Real Intel Mac, Windows, Linux arm64, mobile-native, Firefox, and Safari execution/goldens are not all continuously covered.
entries.future_plan: Execute reproducible cross-target goldens on real hosts and browsers for the full design/00-constraints.md matrix without mixing non-dedicated macOS/Windows timings into benchmark history.

entries.name: Koto-shaped facade
entries.state: Builder, typed eval/exec, a composable load/source_name/environment builder with eval/eval_live/eval_serde/exec/install terminals, public error diagnostic accessors, global insertion, exports, graph-preserving rooted live Value/Table/Function handles with snapshot-free serde, a live globals handle, quota-aware table construction, owned-key/live-value insertion, host-owned require resolution with fresh installation cohorts, atomic module installation, a typed HostSchema/HostContext invocation surface, bounded record transactions, usage receipts, an epoch-safe decision reset, environment presets (standard/deterministic/live) with stdout and determinism-labeled service sockets, examples, and a first koto-to-rustia migration guide exist.
entries.future_plan: Stabilize names and error types; add safe function construction; then expand migration guidance.

entries.name: Owned value firewall
entries.state: OwnedValue supports nil, booleans, numbers, UTF-8 strings, tree-shaped tables, scalar/Option/Vec/BTreeMap conversions, and typed table helpers. It deliberately remains an acyclic snapshot and reports cycles rather than losing graph identity; the separate live layer carries binary strings, buffers, vectors, opaque identity, rich keys, and shared/cyclic tables.
entries.future_plan: Keep the owned layer small and explicit while stabilizing its conversion diagnostics; use rooted live handles whenever payload or graph fidelity matters.

entries.name: Live value handles
entries.state: Rooted VM/epoch-safe Value, Table, and Function handles preserve binary strings, buffers, vectors, rich identity-bearing keys, shared/cyclic tables, mutation, iteration, raw equality, and snapshot-free serde deserialization without exposing collector lifetimes. Live globals, quota-aware table construction, owned-key/live-value insertion, and the composable chunk builder build and execute against identity-bearing host graphs; hardened leaves reject those authorities before allocation or compilation. Live arguments/results cross ordinary and typed invocations, and focused tests cover collector rooting, cross-VM rejection, reset invalidation, rich payloads, cycles, shared identity, profiles, quotas, custom lexical environments, serde, and export access.
entries.future_plan: Controlled-client synchronous callback integrations are verified. Define a concrete public userdata registration contract after the stronger stack-diagnostics pass.

entries.name: Typed host functions
entries.state: Shared HostFunction definitions support disposable create_function values, persistent register_function bindings, and HostModule::function namespaces with owned/live typed arguments and mixed tuple results through arity 8. Heap-owned callbacks are reclaimed after their final reachable guest reference; reset releases disposable captures while rebuilding persistent configuration, and replacement preserves old guest aliases without an append-only registry. Typed VMs retain sealed Input, Slots, Effects, SlotWrites, and profile-gated HostMut views, metadata, explicit fuel, fallible results, panic containment, and named conversion errors. Quota admission and namespace installation are atomic; hardened leaves reject disposable construction.
entries.future_plan: Keep tightening diagnostics and decide whether public signature metadata should grow beyond Rust type names.

entries.name: Extension/linker layer
entries.state: Global and namespaced extension batches install atomically after deterministic registration validation. Coarse capabilities, pre-install function metadata including host-fuel ABI version, Rust parameter/return type names, fallibility, and explicit external-state helpers exist.
entries.future_plan: Add migration docs and decide how much internal fuel schedule data should become public.

entries.name: Public host-bridge seam
entries.state: A lifetime-independent HostSchema and freshly borrowed HostContext provide the generic worker-local boundary without public grabby types, boxed/stored context, locks, Any, raw pointers, Send, or a static context. Sealed capability views expose frozen input/slots or a private bounded effect journal; one invocation shares fuel across guest calls; successful records receive dense sequence numbers; per-handler savepoints and an outer transaction cover execution, snapshotting, and conversion; hard resource failures abort; panics from every VM-controlled host callout roll back records and poison the VM until reset. Injectable output/time providers, VM memory telemetry, logical-live limits, and decision reset are also implemented.
entries.future_plan: Prove the complete boundary under long-running host integration and keep the callback-capture/interior-mutability trust boundary explicit.

entries.name: Module loading and resolution
entries.state: Atomic CompiledModule installation, host-owned replacement, and script-visible require are implemented. ServiceModuleResolver keeps resolution in host policy with no ambient filesystem; the host supplies canonical identity and source. Each installation has a fresh lazy cache cohort shared by its dependency graph and selected by function origin; old rooted functions retain old cohorts, and unreachable cohorts are collector-pruned. Failure restores guest heap/global/coroutine/RNG/logical-time/GC/cache state and provisional roots. Nested referrers, cycles, shared fuel, reset, deterministic labels, panic poisoning, quota admission, INSTALL_TRANSACTION_ABI_VERSION, and MODULE_RESOLUTION_ABI_VERSION are covered. Required modules still cross a non-yieldable native boundary.
entries.future_plan: Add a yieldable require continuation and longer dependency-graph integration evidence.

entries.name: Decision lifecycle and reset
entries.state: Reset ABI v1 is public at VM and facade layers and is restricted to idle decision boundaries. It preserves configuration, services, extensions, installed host functions/modules, lifetime peaks, and host-owned immutable CompiledModule values; discards all guest globals, heap objects, coroutines, programs, caches, diagnostics, coverage, and roots; restarts RNG, logical time, instruction counters, and deterministic GC scheduling; and epoch-invalidates every Value, Table, Function, Exports, and RetainedValue lease. A focused native mixed table/string/coroutine/program/retained-export workload holds exact VM-owned memory statistics after warmup through 600 decisions. The shared native/Node-V8 mixed-heap test adds 96 decision epochs and checks bounded public roots, weak/cyclic reclamation, module replacement, quota/OOM recovery, stale handles, exact post-reset VM statistics, and stable warmed wasm linear-memory pages.
entries.future_plan: Add external dedicated-Linux long-running-host evidence and keep the reset plus typed-invocation contracts stable.

entries.name: Serde bridge
entries.state: Owned-value serde remains the eager acyclic validation and serialization path. Rooted Value, Table, and Exports handles now deserialize directly into DeserializeOwned targets without a recursive OwnedValue snapshot; VM/epoch checks, cycles, depth, exact numeric conversions, table shape, externally tagged enums, typed host VMs, native memory stability, and both wasm adapter lanes are covered.
entries.future_plan: Keep the owned and live formats aligned; add opt-in rich binary/buffer adapters or direct live serialization only when a concrete caller fixes their semantics.

entries.name: Retained handles
entries.state: Script Value, Table, Function, and Exports handles are true collector roots. They retain VM identity and decision epoch, can be exchanged across live calls, and fail closed after reset or when used with another VM. Repeated slot reuse cannot make stale handles alias replacement objects or programs; successful module replacement does not invalidate old rooted handles, and old functions keep their originating dependency cohort.
entries.future_plan: Keep VM and epoch failures explicit as optional userdata and scheduling interfaces are designed.

entries.name: Transactional module replacement
entries.state: Compilation is VM-independent, installation is atomic, and the host swaps its active Exports only after success. Tests cover source-name diagnostics, public runtime-location accessors, failed-candidate old-program survival, shared-graph/upvalue/buffer/metatable/RNG/logical-time/GC/weak-table rollback, quota recovery, typed nested savepoints, per-install dependency cohorts, epoch invalidation on decision reset, and reclamation/reuse of obsolete bytecode, constants, caches, and coverage after the final reachable reference drops.
entries.future_plan: Add broader dependency-graph integration evidence and finish stack diagnostics.

entries.name: Macro/codegen sugar
entries.state: Macro sugar exists as an early slice, but the lower-level API should lead.
entries.future_plan: Delay expansion until the core API stops moving.

entries.name: Harness CLI and schema
entries.state: bench/ has a standalone-style CLI, package metadata, machine-readable inventory, validated JSONL history schema, refreshable RESULTS.md, current-results JSON, generated per-workload claim gating, retained fixed-work A/B evidence, and a separate paired many-VM memory evidence schema.

A coherent 990-process cross-engine memory baseline and the 99-sample safe-memory Rustia refresh are committed.

entries.name: History and static report
entries.state: A coherent Linux-only speed snapshot covers 12 adapter families plus verified mlua/Luau JIT. The generated dashboard includes ranked speed bars, workload heatmaps, performance history, three memory workload cohorts, and Rustia peak/retained history versus a fixed mlua/JIT reference. The current memory view preserves frozen competitor rows while refreshing Rustia from safe-memory-588b541.

entries.name: Benchmark operations
entries.state: Hosted CI validates committed artifacts without provisioning billed infrastructure. An operator can manually start a Rustia-only Linode memory cohort for an exact commit already present on main. The explicit bounded Linode lifecycle promotes only complete evidence after confirmed instance deletion. The cgroup-v2 memory supervisor/analyzer, current/history merge, dashboard, frozen 990-process cross-engine baseline, 99-sample safe-memory Rustia refresh, and wasm32 quota probe are implemented.
entries.future_plan: Keep the Linode lifecycle reproducible, accumulate coherent external allocator/RSS history, and add regression alerts without mixing developer-machine timings.

entries.name: Wasm-emit JIT spike
entries.state: Runtime wasm emission is validated in spikes, not production-integrated.
entries.future_plan: Add type guards/deopt and interpreter-equivalence checks before production use.

entries.name: Native/wasm matrix
entries.state: A coherent 12-adapter-family native Linux baseline plus a verified mlua/Luau JIT mode is recorded; recurring wasm target results cover rustia+koto+rhai and br_table/call_ref dispatch on Node/V8, hosted CI executes the rustia wasm host adapters on Node 22/V8, and the accepted four-runtime matrix remains archived as historical portability evidence.

entries.name: CLI
entries.state: rustia-cli supports file, stdin, --eval, and --repl execution with profile, fuel, and source-name options; state-preserving line evaluation and expression shorthand; source-aware compile/runtime diagnostics; and a fixed-order filesystem require adapter with canonical cache identities, nested referrer-relative resolution, and module-source runtime diagnostics. Deterministic CLI execution deliberately has no ambient filesystem resolver.
entries.future_plan: Add richer multiline editing/history behavior and stack-aware diagnostic formatting; keep filesystem resolution policy stable and covered across supported hosts.

entries.name: Crate publishability
entries.state: Workspace crates are still publish = false, but generated crate metadata audit, explicit internal dependency versions, publishability-derived leaf package dry-run checks in preflight/CI, package file-list audit, publishability blocker audit, release checklist, semver policy, changelog validation, and release preflight are present.
